sentences.text: Revenue went from essentially nil in FY2021 to $5.39 billion in FY2025, a 48.1% three-year CAGR from FY2022 [F3][F7][D342].
The step change came in FY2022, when revenue rose 2914.5% to $1.66 billion on deliveries of 19,412 vehicles [D83][F4][P67].
Growth then decelerated sharply, from 167.4% in FY2023 to 12.1% in FY2024 and 8.4% in FY2025 [D135][D187][D239].
The operating loss narrowed every year after FY2022, from $6.86 billion in FY2022 to $3.59 billion in FY2025, and gross margin turned positive at 2.7% [F23][F26][F19].
In FY2025 Software and Services contributed 21.6pp of the 8.4% revenue growth, while Automotive subtracted 13.2pp [D323][D239][D316].

Software and services revenue rose 221.7% to $1.56 billion, which the filing attributes to vehicle electrical architecture and software development services for the Joint Venture, remarketing and repair and maintenance [D322][S26][P18].
Automotive revenue fell 14.6% to $3.83 billion, primarily on 9,332 fewer deliveries after the 45W tax credits expired, partly offset by higher average selling prices [D315][S23][P22].
Operating costs grew 1.5pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at 6.9%, and incremental operating margin was 264.7% [D266][D258][D265].
Diluted shares rose 17.1% while the net loss shrank 23.2%, so EPS improved 34.5% to -$3.07 [D260][D241][D243][F57].
Operating margin of -66.5% in FY2025 is the window high, far above the -129.4% median and the -7672.7% low of FY2021 [F31][D325][D326][D324].
Gross margin of 2.7% is also the window high against a -45.8% median [F19][D331][D332].
The FY2025 operating margin improved 27.8pp, with cost of revenue adding 26.8pp as it fell 15.0% on fewer vehicles produced and lower material and conversion costs [D253][D267][D255][P21].
SG&A was the one drag, subtracting 0.5pp as it grew 9.9% on go-to-market expansion and higher payroll and stock-based compensation [D269][D257][P13].
In FY2025 net margin of -67.7% sat 1.1pp below the -66.5% operating margin, with other expense of $54 million including a $186 million litigation settlement [F43][F31][D359][X84][P10].
Operating cash flow of -$779 million in FY2025 was far better than the -$4.87 billion FY2023 level, and free cash flow was -$2.49 billion against a net loss of $3.65 billion [F64][F62][F78][F38].
The FY2025 improvement in operating cash flow was primarily driven by a significant reduction in net loss [D244][P4].
Free cash flow margin of -46.2% is the window high but still far below the 6.6% peer median [D226][D334][D348].
Capex rose 49.9% to $1.71 billion, 31.7% of revenue and 2.18x D&A, on Normal Factory capacity expansion [D246][F71][D225][D228][P3].
Net cash fell to $1.64 billion in FY2025 from $16.9 billion in FY2021, as cash and investments dropped 21.0% to $6.08 billion against $4.44 billion of debt [D231][D39][D261][D229][D230].
Net cash was 30.5% of revenue, and the current ratio fell to 2.33x, the window low, from a 4.94x median [D232][F129][D339][D341].
Financing brought in $886 million, primarily from $750 million of Class A shares issued to Volkswagen Group on the Financial Milestone [F92][P2].
Cash and investments cover 2.4 years of the latest burn, and the diluted share count rose 17.1% [D236][D260].
Net losses have persisted for seven straight years, from -$426 million in FY2019 to -$3.65 billion in FY2025 [R1][F32][F38].
The loss is narrowing but the accumulated deficit of $27.0 billion shows how much capital the model has consumed [P5].
Stock-based compensation was 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last five years [R2][D223][D31][D67][D119][D171].
At 20.7% of the operating loss, it is a real cost that flatters cash burn relative to the income statement [D237].
New electric vehicles were 67.6% of revenue and fell 12.5% in FY2025 [R4][D286][D287].
The core vehicle business is shrinking while the growth comes from lower-volume software and Joint Venture services, which is a concentration risk [D293].
Whether gross margin holds above the 2.7% FY2025 level in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the cost trend [F19].
Whether operating cash flow improves past the -$779 million FY2025 level as R2 deliveries begin in Q2 2026 [F64][P31].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue stays above the 30.5% FY2025 level or falls toward zero as capex continues [D232][F71].
